import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 347

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/347](https://www.erdosproblems.com/347)
-/

open Filter Set Topology

namespace Erdos347

/--
The set of subset sums of a set `A ⊆ ℕ`.
-/
local notation "𝓟" A => subsetSums A

/--
Is there a sequence $A=\{a_1\leq a_2\leq \cdots\}$ of integers with
$$\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=2$$
such that
$$P(A')= \left\{\sum_{n\in B}n : B\subseteq A'\textrm{ finite }\right\}$$
has density $1$ for every cofinite subsequence $A'$ of $A$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by ebarschkis in the comments (based on idea of Tao and
van Doorn, also in the comments).

This was formalized in Lean by Barschkis using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/ebarschkis/ErdosProblem/blob/main/Problem347/Formalization.lean"]
theorem erdos_347 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, (Monotone a) ∧
      (Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∧
      (∀ ι : ℕ → ℕ, (range ι)ᶜ.Finite → HasDensity (𝓟 (range (a ∘ ι))) 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos347

reformulations.difference: Cofinite subsequences are represented by arbitrary maps ι : ℕ → ℕ with finite complement of their range, without requiring StrictMono ι. The linked proof instead quantifies over cofinite subsets of range a.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The subset-sum condition depends only on range ι, and every cofinite subset of ℕ has a strictly increasing enumeration. Moreover, the ratio limit 2 forces a to be strictly increasing on a tail, so every finite set of values has finite preimage. Consequently, cofinite subsets of values and cofinite subsets of indices give the same condition. Equivalently, it suffices to require density 1 for every tail: each cofinite selection contains a tail, and density 1 passes to supersets. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: The source says a sequence of integers; Lean uses natural-number values and does not explicitly exclude initial zeros.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nondecreasing integer sequence, a nonpositive denominator makes the successive ratio at most 1 (with Lean's zero-denominator value also harmless). Convergence to 2 therefore forces eventual positivity and strict increase. Deleting the finite initial segment preserves the ratio limit and the requirement for every cofinite subsequence, yielding a positive natural-number witness. Conversely, natural-number witnesses embed into the integers, or can first be truncated if positivity is required. Tail positivity was checked in Lean; the complete domain-change equivalence was not separately formalized.

sources_consulted: Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean, Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean, and Mathlib/Order/Filter/Cofinite.lean at the reviewed checkout
review.notes: The sole theorem and local subset-sum notation faithfully state the source problem. The source's affirmative PROVED (LEAN) status matches research solved, answer(True), and the formal_proof record. HasDensity is ordinary natural density; its interval convention differs from the source's {1,…,N} by a negligible endpoint contribution. Boundary tests and equivalence proofs compile successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including rejection of the zero sequence and failure of density 1 for the powers-of-two sequence after deleting its first term. Erdős Problems pages were read through r.jina.ai because direct requests encountered Cloudflare challenges. The linked proof's statement implies the repository statement; no explicit sorry or custom axiom declarations were found. It contains two native_decide calls and targets Lean 4.24.0, so its full proof was not rebuilt with the sandbox's Lean 4.33.1.
